  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth presented a Powerpoint
  presentation on the item providing information on the proposed ballot
  question for the parcel tax measure, the proposed parcel tax
  structure, and the implementation timeline of the parcel tax revenues
  over the course of 10 years.

  Councilmember Hampton  Councilmember Hampton reported that he is participating remotely
  joined the meeting at 6:10  under the Government Code Section 54953.8.3 "just cause"  »

  p.m.  provision on the basis of childcare needs and stated that no one over
  the age of 18 is in the room with him.

  The following individuals spoke in support of a parcel tax measure to
  fund critical fire capital improvement program and infrastructure
  needs, citing the need for emergency preparedness, and/or provided
  other related comments:

  Carlos Jalevera, West Pasadena Residents Association
  Lee Wallace, West Pasadena Residents Association
  Jacky English, West Pasadena Residents Association
  Chein Vu, Altadena resident
  Christiaan Miller, Pasadena Fire Management
  Raffy Bitchakdjian, Pasadena Firefighters
  Christina Terrazas, Local 809

  The following individuals expressed opposition to the proposed
  parcel tax measure, advocated for the City to find alternative
  methods to cover the costs of fund the Fire Department and fire
  infrastructure needs, spoke on the impacts of additional financial
  burden, and/or provided other related comments:

  Aida Dimejian, Pasadena Foothills Association of Realtors
  David Kissinger, Pasadena Foothills Association of Realtors
  Jesus Rojas, Apartment Association of Greater Los Angeles
  Claire Brian, Pasadena resident
  Adam Bray-Ali, Pasadena Foothills Association of Realtors
  Pete Kutzer, Pasadena resident

  Councilmember Hampton expressed support for the staff
  recommendation, while advocating for a 10-year sunset provision to
  allow voters the opportunity to remove or continue the parcel tax.

  Councilmember Masuda expressed support for the proposed parcel
  tax measure and emphasized the importance of modernizing and
  improving City's Fire Department capacity and infrastructure.

  Council Minutes  3  08/03/2026
   In response to Vice Mayor Rivas' inquiry regarding alternative
  methods to fund ongoing operational costs instead of relying on new
  taxes, Interim City Manager Hawkesworth noted that the City has
  been making incremental gains towards the Fire Department 10-year
  Capital Improvement Plan over the years, however, increased
  operational costs have presented challenges based on the City's
  existing revenue structure. Vice Mayor Rivas also expressed support
  to add a 10- or 15-year sunset on the proposed parcel tax.

  Councilmember Cole expressed support for adding a 15-year sunset
  provision to the proposed parcel tax measure. He also advocated for
  reducing the levy to 170 per square foot instead of the proposed 19^,
  citing the need to lessen the financial burden on residents.

  Councilmember Lyon expressed support for putting the proposed
  parcel tax measure on the ballot for the voters to decide, and
  supported adding a sunset provision. He acknowledged the financial
  burden that a parcel tax may impose on commercial buildings but
  noted that the Eaton Fire demonstrated an urgent need for improved
  infrastructure of the City's Fire Department. In response to
  Councilmember Lyon's concerns on how to ensure that the tax
  revenues are only used for the stated purposes, Interim City
  Manager Hawkesworth reported that the measure is structured as a
  special tax, meaning revenues are restricted to be used only for the
  designated purposes, and cannot be transferred to the General
  Fund. He suggested that the City Council can add language to the
  ordinance and certain provisions in the documents identifying
  specific capital projects, such as the retrofitting of Fire Stations 33
  and 37.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with reducing the
  proposed tax amount, noting that anticipated costs tend to increase
  overtime, and stated his support for the proposed funding approach
  as it represents the fairest method of generating new revenue
  available to the City.

  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth elaborated that the proposed
  ordinance to amend the Pasadena Municipal Code, if approved by
  voters (Exhibit A of the Resolution Calling of the Election), already
  provides the guardrails in terms of uses of the proposed parcel tax
  revenues, but the language can be added to further bolster and
  ensure specificity and transparency for use of parcel tax revenues.

  Councilmember Jones expressed support for a 15-year sunset
  provision, a "check-in" with the City Council at year 1 5, and additional
  language that identifies specific projects and provides more
  guardrails to the measure. Interim City Manager Hawkesworth
  suggested the "check-in" be done sooner to evaluate the project
  timeline, provide updates on the status of deliverables, and to allow
  time for City Council and staff to strategize next steps.

Council Minutes  4  08/03/2026
   Councilmember Cole also noted that the proposed ordinance
  language for the special tax has an annual audit requirement that
  would require annual "check-ins" with the City Council, providing
  opportunities for adjustments and public input.

  ORIGINAL MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Jones,
  seconded by Councilmember Cole, to approve the staff
  recommendation, amended to set a 15-year sunset provision and to
  direct staff to add additional language that identifies specific projects
  and provides more guardrails to the measure that ensures parcel tax
  revenues are spent towards the Fire Department and specified fire
  infrastructure needs.

  Councilmember Madison expressed support for the staff
  recommendation, while noting concerns with adding guarantees or
  sunset provisions to the special parcel tax measure. City Attorney
  Bagneris clarified that the proposed ordinance already contains
  guardrails that restrict the use of revenues to specified projects.
  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth added that if a sunset provision
  were added to the proposed tax, it would require the tax to return to
  the voters for renewal or an extension, should additional funds be
  necessary to complete the workplan. City Attorney Bagneris and
  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth advised that any sunset
  provision should align with election year cycles.

  Mayor Gordo highlighted the need for continued investment in public
  safety infrastructure and emergency response services, noting the
  impacts and lessons learned from the Eaton Fire, the need for
  earthquake preparedness in California, potential limitations of mutual
  aid during regional disasters, and maintaining the expected high
  service levels and standards for Pasadena.

 SUBSTITUTE MOTION:  Councilmember Hampton reiterated his desire to set the sunset
  provision at 10 years, and made a substitute motion to approve the
  staff recommendation with a 10-year sunset provision. (Substitute
  motion failed due to lack of second)

  In response to Councilmember Cole's inquiry regarding how the City
  could ensure financing and completion of retrofitting Fire Stations 33
  and 37 within 10 years, Interim City Manager Hawkesworth stated
  that the City Council could adjust their priorities to accelerate the
  reconstruction of the two stations or advance funding from other
  reserves and repay the funds with future tax revenues.

  Councilmember Cole requested a friendly amendment to
  Councilmember Jones' motion, to reduce the sunset period from 15
  years to 10 years, and adding language that prioritizes the retrofit of
  Fire Stations 33 and 37 within the first 10 years.

Council Minutes  5  08/03/2026
   Vice Mayor Rivas expressed concerns regarding the practical
  implications of a shorter 1 0-year sunset provision noting that planned
  projects may not be fully completed before seeking voter renewal.

  Councilmember Lyon also advocated for a longer sunset which
  would allow operational funding to continue even after capital
  investments are completed to fund next stages.

  Councitmember Madison voiced reservations about a sunset
  provision, emphasizing potential challenges with operational funding
  and achieving two-thirds voter approval if the measure is placed on
  the ballot again in the future. He expressed opposition to the friendly
  amendment and support for original motion.

  Mayor Gordo expressed support for a definitive sunset provision with
  a check-in at year 5.

  Councilmember Lyon and Vice Mayor Rivas expressed support for a
  14-year sunset provision in alignment with election year cycles.

  In response to Councilmember Madison's inquiry regarding what
  other operational expenses will be funded by the revenue, Interim
  City Manager Hawkesworth reported that the tax revenue will fund
  two new rescue ambulances, a new fire engine, a new fire truck, and
  year-round brush abatement. Interim City Manager Hawkesworth
  noted that these operational costs reflect the current 10-year capital
  plan, and that future infrastructure and equipment needs will
  inevitably arise beyond that period.

  Councilmember Madison advocated for a 14-year sunset provision,
  citing the inefficiencies of having funding expire in 10 years. He
  proposed an alternative friendly amendment to Councilmember
  Jones' original motion to change the sunset provision from 15 years
  to 14 years.

  In response to Councilmember Jones' inquiry, Interim City Manager
  Hawkesworth reported that the City Council may reduce or eliminate
  the parcel tax and that the tax cannot be later increased without voter
  approval.

  Councilmember Hampton reiterated his support for a 10-year sunset
  provision, stating that for residents already experiencing financial
  burden, a 10-year sunset may be more palatable to voters.

  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth reported that the City's library
  parcel tax will require renewal in 10 years and should the parcel tax
  pass, there is possibility that the renewal of both the Library Parcel
  Tax and the Fire Department and Fire Infrastructure Parcel Tax
  measures would be considered by voters at the same election,
  creating a competitive scenario between both measures for funding.

Council Minutes  6  08/03/2026
   Councilmembers Jones and Cole accepted Councilmember
  Madison's alternative friendly amendment for a 14-year sunset
  provision on the proposed parcel tax measure.
n  AMENDED MOTION:  Following discussion, it was moved by Councilmember Jones,
  seconded by Councilmember Cole, to approve the staff
  recommendation with a 14-year sunset provision and to add specific
  language to the proposed ordinance guaranteeing the seismic
  retrofitting of Fire Stations 33 and 37.

  AYES: Councilmembers Cole, Jones, Lyon, Madison, Masuda,
  Vice Mayor Rivas, Mayor Gordo
  NOES: None
  ABSENT: None
  ABSTAIN: Councilmember Hampton

  For clarification purposes, Interim City Manager Hawkesworth
  reported that the proposed ballot question will be revised, as follows:
  "City of Pasadena 911 Firefighter/Paramedic Emergency
  Medical/Wildfire Preparedness/Response Measure. To help
  maintain fire, paramedic, 911 response; prepare for/ respond to
  wjldfires/earthquakes/medical emergencies; recruit/retain well-
  trained firefighters; maintain lifesaving equipment/fire alert
  communication; shall City of Pasadena's measure annually levy 190
  per square foot of improved property, with low-income senior
  exemption, providing approximately $22,100,000 annually until
  ended by voters, expiring after 14 years, requiring accountability,
  independent audits, oversight, public spending disclosure; all funds
  must be used to support local fire protection/emergency medical
  response services, be adopted?"

  Interim City Manager Hawkesworth also stated that the language for
  the sunset provision will be added to the ordinance as Section
  4.110.240, as follows: "The special parcel tax established by this
  ordinance shall automatically expire 14 years after its effective date
  unless extended by a subsequent ordinance approved by the voters
  of the City of Pasadena. Upon expiration, no further taxes shall be
  levied pursuant to this chapter, and any remaining funds shall be
  used exclusively for the purposes authorized herein until expended."

  PUBLIC COMMENT ON  The following individuals urged the City Council to continue
  MATTERS NOT ON THE  supporting partnerships with Rose Bowl Riders and Myrtle Hill Farm,
